en: Then one should perform the ritual acceptance (adhivāsana) according to the entire procedure previously described, as well as the placement of the jar and the excellent scattering of flowers and other offerings. ||1||
Having consecrated a firm pitcher made of gold, silver, copper, or earth,
one should place within it the auspicious Anantavijaya.
When the water-pot, which constitutes the body of all sacrifices, is situated in the northeastern direction, one should perform the worship of the group of mantras pertaining to the womb (garbha).

Then follows the procedure for the fire-offering and the satiation of the mantras; thereafter is the procedure for the sacrificial porridge (caru), performed either with the Gāyatrī or with the Hṛdaya-mantra.
The wise man should cook the sacrificial oblation (caru) with cow's milk and sixty-four-fold rice grains in the fire of Śiva; once it is well-cooked, he should remove it from the heat. || 5 ||
Having removed that [portion] and then offered the foremost part to the deity,
one should then perform a single oblation with the entire collection of mantras.
Likewise, for chalk, pegs, eagles, scissors, dust, as well as for all [substances] such as clarified butter, and for perfumes, flowers, and so forth; || 7 ||
For all fresh tooth-sticks made from milky trees,
there shall first be sprinkling with water and then touching them with blades of *kuśa* grass.
On the ninth day, together with the fruits;
then, by the god Śrīkaṇṭha, the offering (bali).
Having bowed to the God of gods, one should sprinkle the disciple and others with water purified by mantras. || 10 ||
With the weapon-mantra of the South, he should strike the head of that bound victim with ashes;
then, by means of the words "Release! Release!", he should bring forth the form of Dakṣiṇāmūrti.
Having positioned himself facing north and the disciple facing east, the preceptor should,
with his whole being, perform the touching of the head with kuśa grass in the proper sequence.
Having seated him and touched him with white flowers while reciting the Brahma-mantras,
one should properly worship him with the Gāyatrī mantra, using perfumes, incense, and sacred purifiers.
First, he should drop [the tooth-stick] at the feet; last, he should drop it before the fire of Śiva and the Guru.
After the disciple has done so, the Guru should then give him the remainder of the tooth-stick.
Having obtained the food, one should eat it slowly while facing north;
however, the teacher should finally consume the remainder of the sacrificial porridge (caru).
One should then perform an expiatory rite consisting of an oblation of food offerings into the fire, with eight oblations of clarified butter using the Aghora mantra for the sake of pacification. 16.

Having first dismissed the Lord of the Gods of gods who was stationed in the midst of the fire, the Guru, together with his disciples, should sleep on the ground upon a sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila). 17.
O Brahmins, the consecration of Śiva has now been described by me; let there not be any further useless or obscure talk regarding the common [rite]. 18.

Even the Vyāsokti (the style of Vyāsa) is set aside, and the Samāsokti (the style of conciseness) is desired; and that indeed should be so, provided there is no excessive weightiness of the composition. (19)
Now it is said in brief: the word of Nidhaneshvara has been heard, which is the certain means for achieving various goals and for determining the meaning of words. 20.
Thus ends the twelfth chapter, on the preliminary consecration (*adhivāsana*), in the *Svāyambhuvasūtrasaṅgraha*.
